title: Motor Enclosure Selector
description: Learners recommend a motor enclosure (ODP, TEFC, TEAO, TENV or explosion proof) for ten illustrative fan jobs. The first choice on each job is scored; wrong choices are crossed out and the learner keeps choosing until reaching an accepted enclosure, which reveals the reason. Five reference cards show each enclosure's cooling path and FanPedia's IP and duty mappings; a summary lists each first choice beside the accepted answer.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Choosing a motor enclosure for a fan job
learningObjectives: The learner will recommend a motor enclosure (ODP, TEFC, TEAO, TENV or EXPL) for each of ten described fan jobs, with at least 8 of 10 first-attempt choices falling in the accepted set.
prerequisites: ODP, TEFC, TEAO, TENV and explosion proof motors
intended duty (GD, SD, IEEE 841, IEEE 45, DFG)

rules: One choice per job from the five enclosures; the first choice is correct when it is in the job's accepted set.
Job 1 accepts ODP and TEFC; choosing TEFC adds 'ODP would also have been acceptable here.'
Later choices continue until an accepted enclosure is reached and never change the score.
Mastery is 8 or more of 10 correct on the first attempt.
assumptions: The motor sketches are schematic, not to scale.
limitations: Does not cover NEC class, division and group selection, ATEX motors, or catalog availability of a given enclosure and frame.

sources: Source: FanPedia p. 73 (Motor Specifications: Enclosure and Intended Duty)
Jobs 1, 2, 6 and 9 follow the worked examples in Chapter 14 'Motor Enclosures'

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Committed first choice with reasoned feedback, retry until correct, reference cards for exploration, end-of-round summary
keyQuestions: Is the area classified as hazardous?
What is in the air around the motor?
Does the motor have its own fan, rely on the fan's airstream, or have no fan at all?
commonMisconceptions: ODP is fine anywhere indoors, even in dirty or wet air.
An explosion-proof motor is needed whenever the air is dirty.
A TEAO motor cools itself the way a TEFC motor does.
TENV is simply a better TEFC with no downside.
assessmentOpportunities: First-try score shown as 'First-try correct: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
